operation.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Updates an existing **credit type**.

The record to update is identified by the **`id` field in the request body** (not by a path segment). Include `id` and POST to `/v2/api/entity/credit_type` — the same path as create; supplying `id` switches the operation from insert to update.

**This is a full-row overwrite.** Any writable field omitted from the body is reset to its column default or null (`status`→`1`, `allow_decimal`→`0`, `unit`/`description`→null), so always resend every field you want to keep. `name` is required and must stay **unique**.

Note: a request that puts the id in the path instead (`/credit_type/{id}`) does **not** update — it creates a new record. Always send `id` in the body.

id.description: Required. Id of the credit type to update.

name.description: Required (full-row overwrite). Name of the credit type. Must be unique across your credit types.

allow_decimal.description:
Optional. Whether fractional amounts are allowed. If omitted it resets to `0` (No).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | No |
| 1 | Yes |

status.description:
Optional. Whether the credit type is active. If omitted it resets to `1` (Active).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Inactive |
| 1 | Active |

unit.description: Optional. Unit label shown for the credit. If omitted it resets to null.

description.description: Optional. Free-text description. If omitted it resets to null.

message.description: Localized message (may read "added" even on update).

id.description: Id of the updated credit type.

400.description: The record could not be saved. This occurs when `name` is omitted (a full-row overwrite would write null) or duplicates another credit type name (names are unique) — the endpoint has no field-level validation, so the underlying database error is returned.

e.description: Raw database error context (error info array, connection name, read/write type).

error.description: Database error detail explaining why the row could not be saved.

401.description: The access token is missing, invalid, or expired. A caller who is authenticated but lacks update permission for this entity also receives a `401` with a message stating access is not allowed.
